insights.topic: Verified purchase proof vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl's cryptographically verified receipts confirm purchases happened — not inferred from browsing behavior. At a ~$0.10/receipt floor and 96,000+ confirmed receipts, this is a functioning deterministic signal layer, not a pilot.

insights.topic: Grocery and mass retail dominate verified receipt volume
insights.insight: Walmart (306 receipts), Kroger (146), Costco (136), and Safeway (136) account for the heaviest verified purchase concentration in the 14-day window — these are the exact retailers where CPG and FMCG brands need post-purchase confirmation, not cookie-based inference.

insights.topic: Retail outspends grocery on average ticket despite fewer receipts
insights.insight: Retail-department-stores generated $30,443 GMV across 698 receipts versus grocery-supermarkets at $58,481 across 1,343 receipts — retail's per-receipt average is running roughly 2.4x grocery's, a durable pattern across multiple observation windows that matters for brands measuring verified basket size.

insights.topic: Token velocity acceleration is a leading demand signal
insights.insight: Week-over-week velocity sits at 0.557x — below replacement rate — but acceleration has posted above 1.2x for two consecutive morning readings, the highest sustained streak on record. Acceleration leading absolute velocity is the pattern to watch for timing audience-scale commitments.

insights.topic: Digital commerce receipts in the verified pool
insights.insight: The DKIM vendor surface includes Amazon, Stripe, Paddle, Gumroad, Suno, and OpenAI alongside physical retail — meaning verified purchase signals span both brick-and-mortar and digital subscription/software spend, broadening the addressable audience beyond in-store shoppers.

insights.topic: Geographic coverage is active but contracting
insights.insight: Metro coverage declined from 20 cells at peak to 17 active aggregate cells in the current snapshot, with cells dropping below the visibility threshold outpacing new additions — brands building geo-targeted activation plans should treat current metro availability as dynamic, not fixed.
